fundamental.text: Raw sugar is 2.00¢/lb above hydrous-ethanol parity in Brazil, so mills favour sugar in the mix (more supply). Sugar in BRL at R$2,314/t (59th pct of 5 yrs). Raws slipped below 18 cents on 18 Nov after USDA's biennial outlook and a weak real; producer hedging stays light, but speculative length is still large, so the band's floor is being tested rather than defended. Desk read: Brazil still drives it: the weaker real makes Brazilian raws cheaper to sell abroad and sugar keeps paying over hydrous ethanol, so mills stay sugar-heavy. USDA's lower global production estimate is a mild offset, but it has not stopped Mar slipping to the 18.0 support area.
